column1: # AMD CPU only. Selected by $CPU_VENDOR in bootstrap.sh, not by machine.
# NB: there is no AMD counterpart to thermald and none is needed - k10temp is
# in-tree and the SMU manages boost itself. What AMD desktops DO need is a
# sensor driver the kernel does not ship, below.
# NB: nct6687d-dkms-git is NOT an AMD-CPU fact and does not really belong here.
# It is a MOTHERBOARD fact - the Nuvoton Super-I/O chip on MSI B450/B550 boards -
# and there is no board axis, so it rides the CPU axis because on the two
# machines this repo has, "AMD CPU" and "that MSI board" are the same machine.
# lib/detect.sh's own warning applies to this row: folding two facts into one
# axis is how a third machine gets the wrong answer. Concretely, an AMD LAPTOP
# would build this DKMS module every kernel bump for a chip it does not have.
# That is wasteful, not broken, so it is not worth inventing a fourth axis for -
# but the genuinely broken direction (an Intel DESKTOP getting a modules-load.d
# entry for a module nothing installed, failing systemd-modules-load at every
# boot) IS closed, in system/apply.sh, which now also requires the module to
# exist. Add a board axis here only if a third machine actually arrives.

column5: `sensors` and the detection helper. On its own it finds k10temp (CPU die) and nothing else - fan RPM and board voltages need the driver on the next row

out-of-tree driver for the Nuvoton chip on MSI B450/B550 boards (B450M Mortar MAX included). The IN-TREE nct6683 binds the same chip but is read-only and reports nothing useful; nct6687 is the one that exposes fan1_input and pwm control. system/apply.sh installs the modules-load.d drop-in that actually loads it. NB: DKMS, so it rebuilds on every kernel bump - if `sensors` goes quiet after an update, check `dkms status` first
